Here, we propose a quantum extreme learning-based framework for quantum parameter estimation which avoids the explicit construction of the likelihood function. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach using the transverse-field Ising model for estimating the external transverse field. Our results show that high estimation accuracy can be achieved using measurements at only a small number of training points. We further develop an interrogation-time optimization strategy that minimizes the estimation inaccuracy while keeping sampling fluctuations below a prescribed threshold. We further extend the framework to a two-time measurement protocol, in which measurement outcomes obtained at two distinct times are combined to enrich the feature space, thereby significantly enhancing the estimation accuracy. Our analysis shows that the estimation precision improves monotonically with the number of training points, while increasing the system size generally enhances the sensing performance, albeit non-monotonically. Finally, the protocol is shown to be robust against dephasing, making it suitable for near-term quantum devices.
item.dc:creator: Dingwei Zhao, Srijon Ghosh, Victor Montenegro, Matteo G. A. Paris, Marco G. Genoni, Abolfazl Bayat

item.title: Structure makes quantum circuits trainable
item.description: arXiv:2611.18378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The scalability of variational quantum algorithms is limited by barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially in system size. This worst-case result raises fundamental questions about the trainability of quantum AI models. We present a major advance towards resolving this trainability question by answering whether a given quantum circuit has a barren plateau. We do this using an analytical framework that bounds the gradient variance for arbitrary input states $\rho$ and observables $\mathcal{M}$ by decomposing the unitary representation of the associated compact Lie group. When the circuit segments on both sides of a gate form $2$-designs, we obtain the variance exactly and prove a sufficient condition for trainability: if $\rho^{\otimes 2}$ and $\mathcal{M}^{\otimes 2}$ are sufficiently concentrated on the same irreducible invariant subspace of polynomial dimension, and the differentiated gate moves this subspace by an inverse-polynomial amount, then the gradient variance is at least inverse-polynomial. We further present a sampling algorithm that estimates the gradient variance from runs of the ansatz, without constructing the representation-theoretic projectors. Our algorithm decides whether the variance exceeds a tolerance $\tau$ with the number of runs polynomial in $1/\tau$, including cases in which the bounds are inconclusive. This resolves the question of the trainability of the circuit before expensive training procedures.
item.dc:creator: Wenbo Xie, Wojciech Szpankowski, Ananth Grama

item.title: Quantum computational spectroscopy of complex resonances and optical residues
item.description: arXiv:2611.18388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical spectra of dissipative molecular systems depend on both complex resonance energies and the way each resonance couples to an optical probe. In a non-Hermitian description, these con- tributions are determined by complex residues involving left and right eigenvectors. We introduce a quantum protocol that reconstructs the resonance poles and their biorthogonal optical residues within a common spectral-filtering and measurement framework. A Hermitian dilation embeds the left and right eigenvectors into a zero-energy subspace. Gaussian-filtered correlators evaluated with unitary circuits, together with ratios of complex off-diagonal measurements, yield the residues with- out separate variational optimisation of the eigenstates. We demonstrate spectral reconstruction for dissipative plasmon-molecule models on IBM quantum hardware, resolving how probe-dependent modal contributions produce interference-induced doublets or accompany a separation of resonance energies. We also analyse the sensitivity of residue reconstruction near exceptional points. By mak- ing complex optical residues an explicit computational output, the protocol connects non-Hermitian eigenstructure to measurable optical response.
item.dc:creator: Payman Mahmoudi, Jiate Luo, Chonghao Zhai, Qiang Shi, Alexander Yosifov, Jinzhao Sun

item.title: Number fluctuations and particle loss in Dicke superradiance
item.description: arXiv:2611.18413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dicke superradiance, the collective spontaneous emission of identical quantum emitters into a common reservoir, produces a burst with a characteristic delay $t_{\mathrm{SR}}$ and a peak intensity that scales quadratically with the emitter number $N$. This strong dependence makes the burst sensitive to how many emitters actually participate. In experiments, however, this number is rarely fixed: it fluctuates between preparations and decreases during emission through atom loss. Here we extend the analytical treatment of superradiance to variable emitter numbers using the Schwinger-boson mapping of the collective spin onto two bosonic modes. In this formulation, collective decay annihilates an atom in the excited-state mode and creates one in the ground-state mode. We find that number fluctuations enhance emission and that the ensemble-averaged emission trace encodes the initial number distribution. We show how to reconstruct second-order correlations from photon counting with finite detection efficiency and temporal resolution, even when the full distribution cannot be resolved. For atom loss at rate $r$, we derive exact results for the population dynamics and show that the peak intensity scaling is governed by the single scaling variable $g_{\mathrm{r}}=r t_{\mathrm{SR}}$. The peak remains quadratic in $N$ for $g_{\mathrm{r}}<1$, follows logarithmically corrected subquadratic power laws for $g_{\mathrm{r}}>1$, and crosses over to linear scaling under strong loss with $g_{\mathrm{r}}\gg1$.
item.dc:creator: Christian Niehof, Nico S. Bassler, Claudiu Genes

item.title: Tessa: Encoding Classical Data Across an Entire Quantum Processor
item.description: arXiv:2611.18440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Tessa, a hardware-aware, device-wide scheme to encode classical data on quantum computers. We use it to experimentally encode and decode up to $1568$ real values using IBM's Phoenix and Fez quantum computers on a variety of data. Tessa's construction is an extension of QPIXL and QCrank. However, it checkerboards address and data qubits across a coupling graph with neighbouring data qubits sharing only a subset of address qubits. When using the device's coupling graph no SWAP gates or routing is required, but the construction works for any bipartite coupling graph. The shots required for readout are determined by the local coupling degree. As examples, we have used cat states (pixel art of cats), various pixel art, audio, MIDI, DNA sequences and protein amino acid sequences.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Bultrini

item.title: Nesting in additive manufacturing using quantum annealing
item.description: arXiv:2611.18447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nesting in powder bed fusion (PBF), an additive manufacturing (AM) process, determines the positions and orientations of parts within the build space and influences build height and build time. As the number of parts and feasible placements increases, the nesting problem becomes computationally demanding. Exact approaches are limited to small problem sizes as computational effort increases rapidly with the problem size, while heuristic and metaheuristic approaches involve a trade-off between solution quality and computation time. Quantum annealing (QA) offers an alternative for solving combinatorial optimization problems, but its application to nesting in AM remains largely unexplored. This paper presents a QA-based approach for nesting in AM to investigate its feasibility and its scaling behavior across three problem sizes. An iterative binary quadratic model based approach (IBQM) is developed to minimize build height while considering the geometric characteristics of AM parts. Geometric abstraction, iterative decomposition, and variable pruning are applied to address the computational complexity of the nesting problem. The approach is evaluated using three cases with increasing problem sizes and compared to a classical approach combining tabu search and simulated annealing (TBSA). Compared with TBSA, IBQM reduces the build height of the original parts by up to 13.32% and the computation time by up to 74.27%.
item.dc:creator: Xiangqian Wua, Jannik Gayer, Marcel Wagner, Jan C. Aurich

item.title: Learning observable propagation with sparse local moments
item.description: arXiv:2611.18448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a unified framework for predicting local moment dynamics in high-dimensional many-body systems from short-time trajectories. Thanks to the locality of the dynamics, we construct the transition moment matrices by projecting the Markov operator onto low-order connected-cluster basis functions supported near the target observable. Exploiting the spatial decay of time-lagged correlations, {these matrices} can be approximated in sparse-plus-low-rank form using trajectory samples, with computational cost scaling linearly in the system dimension and the number of trajectories. The learning error can be further reduced by correcting the memory effect induced by the Galerkin projection. We numerically demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in extrapolating the dynamics of various many-body systems, including Langevin and Glauber dynamics for classical systems as well as Lindblad dynamics for open quantum systems. In addition, for a class of single-site Glauber dynamics, we establish error bounds for sparse-plus-low-rank compression and uniform-in-time bounds for connected-cluster approximation and observable propagation with compressed transition moment matrices.
item.dc:creator: Yuehaw Khoo, Bowen Li, Yuguan Wang, Siyao Yang

item.title: Symmetry-Controlled Quantum State Transfer in Poly-bi-[8]-annulenylene: From Heisenberg to Hubbard Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.18457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate quantum state transfer in the poly-bi-[8]-annulenylene lattice using isotropic Heisenberg and Hubbard models. For a 16-site lattice, reflection symmetry separates the single-excitation Hamiltonian into independent triplet and singlet sectors, allowing analytical determination of the energy spectra. Although perfect state transfer is forbidden for positive couplings, appropriately chosen coupling ratios enable pretty-good transfer with arbitrarily high fidelity. Remarkably, the triplet transfer probability is independent of the interchain rung coupling, while singlet transfer can be selectively enhanced or suppressed, enabling symmetry-selective quantum transport without time-dependent control. Extending the analysis to the Hubbard model, we show that the Heisenberg transfer dynamics emerge in the strong-interaction limit, while finite interactions delay all high-fidelity transfer peaks of a symmetry sector by the same fraction of their transfer time, set by the spectrum, and reduce the peak fidelity, even at the corrected time, by an amount that grows with the transfer time. These findings are relevant to future quantum-network architectures, where symmetry-controlled state transfer could provide a building block for connecting quantum memories and emitter-based interfaces within quantum nodes. Overall, our results demonstrate how molecular network geometry and symmetry can be exploited to engineer and control quantum-state transport in interacting spin systems, providing a theoretical framework for quantum information transfer in molecular-inspired quantum architectures.
item.dc:creator: Adnan Jaljuli, Pablo Serra, Ammar Ali, Sabre Kais

item.title: Dissipation as a Resource for Entanglement via High-Spin Mediator Purification
item.description: arXiv:2611.18489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study entanglement generation between two spin qubits mediated by a single, thermally mixed, high-spin ($S=5/2$) magnetic impurity, using the Lindblad master equation to compare coherent and dissipative control of the mediator. We show that no coherent drive, however strong or resonant, can purify the mediator beyond its thermal value --- a direct consequence of unitary evolution exactly preserving state purity --- while a dissipative channel purifies it up to the limit set by the optical pumping cycle itself, $\mathrm{Tr}[\rho_M^2]\approx0.8$. Modeling this channel with rates fixed by the measured optical pumping of a single Mn spin, we find that the entanglement it enables is not monotonic in the pump strength: it peaks at a finite rate and then decreases, since the same channel leaks decoherence to the qubits through the coupling that mediates their entanglement. At the experimental pumping rate, a single $80$ns pulse purifies the mediator, the resulting polarization persists for a timescale three orders of magnitude longer than the entangling dynamics, and the first-recurrence negativity rises from $0.18$ to $0.64$ at $12$K, remaining above $0.6$ up to $30$K. These results establish dissipation, not as noise to be suppressed, but as the very resource that makes robust entanglement generation possible.
item.dc:creator: Ellen Martins Fernandes, Fabricio Macedo de Souza

item.title: Solution of the Qubit Marginal Problem from Fermionic Representability
item.description: arXiv:2611.18503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whether local reduced states are compatible with a global quantum state---the quantum marginal problem---is central to quantum information and simulation. Here we present a solution to the ensemble marginal problem for qubits based on the representability theory of fermions. Encoding each qubit as one fermion in two orbitals, we prove that the representable qubit marginals form an exposed face of the set of $N$-representable fermionic reduced density matrices, selected by the vanishing of every site-occupation variance. Complete hierarchies of fermionic representability conditions therefore transfer exactly to qubits. Applications to frustrated Heisenberg and transverse-field Ising rings show that the $(2,3)$-positivity conditions are exact at the Majumdar--Ghosh point and accurate to about 0.5% at criticality. Because the conditions hold for any quantum state, they also provide a framework for mitigating measurement errors on qubit-based quantum devices.
item.dc:creator: David A. Mazziotti

item.title: Agentic AI for Discovering Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
item.description: arXiv:2611.18504v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scaling quantum computing toward practical quantum advantage is currently limited by the efficiency of circuits that operate on information encoded by quantum error-correcting codes. The full stack of quantum computing encompasses several tasks: preparation of logical code states, implementation of logical gates, logical routines on encoded qubits, etc. Yet, these circuits are largely designed by hand for individual cases, with some recent works incorporating machine learning for certain aspects. We formulate this problem as agentic evolutionary program synthesis, wherein a large language model, leveraging its pretraining knowledge and tool-use proficiency, and guided by a circuit verifier, evolves a program that defines a Clifford circuit for a wide range of curated tasks such as logical state preparation, logical gate design, and logical routines such as code-switching, code growth, etc. Our approach consistently finds fault-tolerant circuits for all of these tasks, each verified by an exhaustive check over faults.
item.dc:creator: Aritra Lahiri, Florian Marquardt

item.title: Complex fluid flow dynamics by bright scattershot boson sampling
item.description: arXiv:2611.18510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Boson sampling machines have become a fruitful tool for establishing new concepts, which connect fundamental physics with computer science applications. Here, we exploit the intrinsically high-dimensional correlations generated by the measurement outcomes of a multiphoton boson sampling machine and demonstrate how a reconfigurable architecture can be programmed to autonomously model the time evolution of nonlinear dynamical systems that describe complex fluid flows. By extending on the original scattershot boson sampling (SBS) scheme to include higher photon number components -- a scheme which we label bright scattershot boson sampling (BSBS) --- this scheme overcomes scaling issues inherent to SBS-based schemes by utilizing all randomly generated input photon number distributions. We illustrate the capability of this scheme for two complex fluid-flow models: an eight-dimensional Lorenz-type model of two-dimensional thermally driven convection and a 16-dimensional model of global atmospheric circulation. Using a digital twin of the BSBS architecture based on multiphoton statistics, we show that the photonic approach accurately reproduces the temporal dynamics of both systems while being resilient to photon losses of up to 50 per cent. We also verified that the BSBS case outperforms a comparable run with coherent light. Moreover, its prediction horizon exceeds that of a classical reservoir-computing model with the same query complexity. These results highlight the potential of near-term photonic quantum computing for addressing relevant real-world tasks on noisy intermediate-scale devices.
item.dc:creator: Robert Schade, Shailendra K. Rathor, Tim J. Bartley, Benjamin Brecht, Christian Plessl, Jan Sperling, Michael Stefszky, Christine Silberhorn, J\"org Schumacher

item.title: Real-time simulation of scattering in $\phi^4$ theory: localized excitation, scalable wave packet preparation, and peak-generating artifacts
item.description: arXiv:2611.18552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Probing real-time dynamics is essential for understanding non-perturbative scattering and interactions in quantum field theory. A common challenge in real-time simulation is preparing accurate asymptotic incoming states. Through efficiently solvable eigenvalue problems, we jointly optimize a superposition of single particle momentum eigenstates and a single site interpolating operator to maximize preparation fidelity from the interacting vacuum. This leads to a localized excitation in the interacting theory analogous to a position eigenstate. Weighted sums of the resulting interpolating operator over lattice sites prepare wave packets of arbitrary spatial extent. To ensure that this construction produces the correct continuum limit, relative phases among single particle momentum eigenstates in this superposition are calibrated using a relation derived from Lorentz symmetry. Analyzing single particle wave packet propagation through the position space profile reveals oscillatory Airy distortions, which originate from interference between saddle point contributions at different momenta that share the same lattice group velocity. These oscillations systematically weaken when approaching the continuum limit, and reliable regimes are identified as a function of simulation time and wave packet momentum profile. Two-particle scattering simulations in interacting scalar field theory are also implemented, revealing artificial inelasticity arising from coarse local field digitization or deviation from the Nyquist-Shannon sampling point. With these artifacts under control, present simulations provide emerging evidence for physical inelastic processes in $\phi^4$ theory. The constructions introduced in this work may provide new understanding of state preparation for the quantum simulation of scattering.
item.dc:creator: Boyu Gao, Natalie Klco

item.title: Axis-selective AC magnetic-field imaging in the tens-of-megahertz regime using RF-dressed continuous-wave scanning NV magnetometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.17366v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatially resolved magnetic-field imaging reveals material properties and local currents in microelectronic devices. Conventional pulsed scanning nitrogen-vacancy (NV) magnetometry (SNVM) faces increasingly stringent microwave (MW) pulse-control requirements for detecting radio-frequency (RF) magnetic fields at frequencies ranging from tens to hundreds of megahertz. To address this challenge, we implement an RF-dressed continuous-wave (CW) sensing scheme for SNVM and demonstrate AC magnetic-field imaging at 33.5 MHz. The method exploits electron-spin double resonance in the NV spin-1 three-level system: the target RF magnetic field coherently couples two spin eigenstates, forming RF-dressed states whose splittings are detected in continuous-wave electron-spin double resonance (CW-ESDR) spectra under continuous laser, MW, and RF excitation. This approach avoids short, high-power MW pulses and synchronization between the RF field and a pulsed sensing sequence. Using an NV-ensemble diamond probe integrated with an atomic force microscope (AFM), we image the Oersted field of an RF-driven L-shaped microcircuit. Successively selecting three crystallographic NV axes by static bias-field control yields maps of RF magnetic-field projection magnitudes, with distinct distributions qualitatively reproduced by Biot-Savart calculations. Transverse bias-field control also tunes the RF-coupled spin-state transition frequency from 14.4 to 89.3 MHz, as characterized by spectroscopy and Hamiltonian analysis, with RF-dressed resonances directly observed in CW-ESDR spectra at 89.3 MHz. Together with previous RF magnetic-field detection up to 632 MHz using the same RF-dressed CW sensing principle in a confocal NV setup, these results support extending AC magnetic-field imaging with SNVM toward the hundreds-of-megahertz regime and, with additional phase information, vector magnetic-field reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Shuntaro Komuro, Ryusei Okaniwa, Kazuma Okura, Kunitaka Hayashi, Toshu An, Junko Ishi-Hayase

item.title: Note on quantum optimal measurements of CMB spectral distortions
item.description: arXiv:2611.17552v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As quantum sensing techniques continue to push the frontier of detection of ultra-weak signals, one may wonder if a sophisticated quantum strategy could be used to enable measurement of spectral distortions in the cosmic microwave background. Using quantum Fisher information techniques, we prove that the optimal strategy is simple frequency-binned intensity measurement. This proof strategy also enables us to provide numerical estimates for the information-theoretic minimum observation time required to observe the $\mu$- and $y$-distortions expected from $\Lambda$CDM cosmology. As case studies, we compare these results to the PIXIE and SPECTER mission concepts, and show that they are within a few orders of magnitude of this fundamental limit.
item.dc:creator: Roshni Singh, Jacques Delabrouille, Daniel Carney

item.title: Red-Blue Hamiltonian Tomography via the Operator Lightcone Wavemap
item.description: arXiv:2611.17555v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a model-free method for Hamiltonian tomography based on the operator spreading wavefront. Given two tensor network simulations of the same quantum lattice (one with the nominal Hamiltonian and one with one or more perturbed bonds), the signed cross-entropy of the non-identity Pauli weight field $\mathcal{L}(v,t) = -\ln(n_{\rm pert}/n_{\rm base})$ identifies each perturbed bond by its causal signature: a red-blue sign flip at the two endpoints, visible from the first wavefront crossing. Combining measurements from $p$ strategically placed observation centers via an ensemble log-likelihood sum, a single broken bond is identified with an 82-fold margin over the next candidate on a $7\times7$ lattice. Extending to realistic coupling degradation ($\delta J = -0.20$) and up to 8 simultaneous faults, the integrated log-ratio $\Lambda(v) = \ln(\mathcal{B}(v)/\mathcal{N}(v))$ achieves a per-bond detection rate above 90\% in a single seismic pass using only 6 simulations. An iterative re-scan strategy progressively resolves multi-bond cases as the signal clears with each recalibration pass. The method requires no model assumptions and no knowledge of the perturbation type or magnitude; the detection is deliberately blind.
item.dc:creator: Paolo D'Alberto

item.title: Compiling Matrix Formulas to Quantum Block Encodings
item.description: arXiv:2611.17756v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Realizing the promise of quantum applications such as chemistry or fluid dynamics requires building quantum circuits that efficiently encode and manipulate exponentially large matrices. This process forces researchers to grapple with the reality that a matrix expressible as one equation on paper can map to thousands of bit-level quantum logic gates, historically written by hand. Even worse, it often ends with a discovery that the needed resources grow so quickly with matrix size that the quantum algorithm loses its asymptotic speedup. In this work, we present MARBLE, a language that automatically synthesizes an efficient circuit from the publication-style formula for the entries of a matrix. MARBLE algebraically rewrites programs into symbolic combinations of simpler matrices that have known circuit realizations. It analyzes costs of possible representations, notably the subnormalization term that dominates time complexity. It then emits an OpenQASM circuit and certifies whether its cost is poly-logarithmic in problem size, as required by quantum algorithms. When evaluated on quantum applications ranging from fluid dynamics to physical Hamiltonians, MARBLE matches or surpasses 37 of 39 published baselines. On the low end, it automatically matches many theoretically optimal circuits, and on the high end, it improves on a published construction in fluid dynamics by 10,487x in subnormalization. MARBLE produces exponentially smaller circuits than the leading tool FABLE, and it successfully compiles matrices whose dimensions exceed 2^100 within five seconds on a laptop.
item.dc:creator: Daksh Shami, Charles Yuan

item.title: Exponential Lower Bounds for the Spherically Averaged Density of Atoms
item.description: arXiv:2611.17969v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of the spherically averaged density $\widetilde \rho$ for fermionic bound states of the $N$-electron atomic Hamiltonian $H_{N,Z}$ with nuclear charge $Z$. For the density associated with an eigenfunction satisfying $H_{N,Z}\psi=E\psi$, we show that if the energy $E$ is below the bottom of the essential spectrum $\Sigma:=\inf\mathop{\rm ess.spec} (H_{N,Z})$, then \[ \lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{\ln \widetilde \rho(r)}{r} =\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{d}{dr}{\ln \widetilde\rho(r)} =-2\alpha_0, \] with $\alpha_0=\sup\{\alpha \ge 0\colon e^{2\alpha r}\widetilde \rho \in L^1(\mathbb{R_+},r^2dr)\}$. The same is true at threshold in certain cases. Moreover, we prove $\alpha_0^2=\Sigma-E$ for the ground states of $H_{3,Z}$ with sufficiently large $Z$.
item.dc:creator: Yukimi Goto

item.title: The Train Unit Shunting Problem with Service Scheduling and Workforce Assignment: classical and quantum optimization approaches
item.description: arXiv:2611.17987v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Efficient railway rolling stock management requires the coordinated planning of train-unit assignment, shunting movements, track occupation, service operations, and workforce allocation. These interdependent decisions give rise to a challenging combinatorial optimization problem, particularly as the size of the fleet and the planning horizon increase. This paper introduces the Train Unit Shunting Problem with Service Scheduling and Workforce Assignment, a mixed-integer linear programming formulation that integrates these operational decisions within a unified optimization framework. To improve computational tractability, a preprocessing procedure is developed to reduce the size of the resulting model. The proposed approach is evaluated through computational experiments on instances of increasing size and under different objective-function weight and cost configurations. Classical optimization experiments using Gurobi show that filtering method reduces the number of decision variables and constraints, while its impact on computational time varies across instances. In addition, a constrained quadratic model representation is investigated using D-Wave's hybrid quantum-classical optimization solver.
item.dc:creator: Alessia Ciacco, Francesca Guerriero, Eneko Osaba

item.title: Quantum tomography of Higgsstrahlung: Higgs boson self-coupling and $Z$ boson anomalous couplings
item.description: arXiv:2611.18136v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Higgs boson self-coupling enters the Higgsstrahlung process $e^+e^-\to ZH$ at one loop. The three diagrams that carry it project onto two Lorentz structures: the tree-level one, which rescales the rate, and that of the CP-even anomalous coupling $b_Z$, which changes the polarization of the final-state $Z$ boson. To assess how well quantum state tomography constrains the $hZZ$ anomalous couplings and the trilinear coupling at FCC-ee, we compute the helicity density matrix of the $Z$ boson, for an effective vertex that also includes a CP-odd anomalous coupling $\tilde b_Z$, together with its complete one-loop correction in the Standard Model. With these corrections and no other new physics in the effective vertex, quantum state tomography determines $\kappa_\lambda$ to $\pm 3.9$, or $\pm 2.9$ with the full angular information, independently of the rate and of the normalization of the vertex, and not far from the limit $\delta\kappa_\lambda \simeq 1$ set by the quantum Fisher information. Without assumptions on the new physics, quantum tomography directly bounds the anomalous couplings at the $10^{-3}$ level, improving on the existing projections. The density matrix also characterizes the $Z$ boson as a qutrit. At $365$ GeV its state in the central region is pure enough to violate the Klyachko--Can--Binicio\u{g}lu--Shumovsky contextuality inequality, $\mathbb{CNTXT}_5 = 2.06$ at $\theta = \pi/2$ against the non-contextual bound $2$. We also quantify the purity and the amount of magic of the $Z$ boson state, using the mana, the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy and the robustness of magic for the latter. At fixed angle, purity, contextuality and magic are robust against anomalous couplings of the size probed by the tomography. The inclusive state, instead, is neither contextual in this test nor magic in the helicity basis.
item.dc:creator: Clelia Altomonte, Marco Fabbrichesi, Niko Koivunen, Luca Marzola, Daniele Rizzo

item.title: Transfer-Matrix Calculus for Infinite Matrix Product States
item.description: arXiv:2611.18427v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-range interactions, from the Coulomb repulsion between electrons to the power-law interactions of trapped ions and Rydberg atoms, are widespread in quantum many-body physics. For infinite systems, however, MPS algorithms, the standard classical reference in one dimension, conventionally rely on a computational compromise: replacing these interactions by fitted sums of exponentials. We develop transfer-matrix calculus (TMC), a unified framework for deriving infinite-MPS algorithms. In TMC, an interaction is written as a function of the transfer matrix, and one set of contraction rules then yields the effective Hamiltonians of DMRG and VUMPS, the tangent-space excitation action, and the energy variance, without an MPO. Long-range interactions thus enter with their prescribed distance dependence. For the half-filled lattice Coulomb chain with a $1/d$ interaction of strength $V$, theory predicts CDW order for all $V>0$, but at weak coupling this order is too weak for earlier numerics to resolve. Using TMC, we obtain infinite-MPS ground states at $V=2$ directly in the thermodynamic limit, with an energy variance per site of $2\times10^{-10}$. Our data, extrapolated to zero energy variance, indicate a small nonzero CDW amplitude, $m_0=0.002213(14)$, consistent with this prediction. The complete $V=2$ optimization workflow across the full series of bond dimensions takes less than a day on a single AMD MI250X GPU die. For an exactly solvable long-range hopping model, TMC reproduces the nonanalytic $|k|$ cusp of the one-particle dispersion that any fixed finite sum of decaying exponentials rounds off. We also use TMC to optimize first-quantized MPS directly in the thermodynamic limit. For half-filled free fermions, our entanglement entropy data show scaling consistent with central charge $c=1$ over the studied bond dimensions, as for second-quantized MPS.
item.dc:creator: Qi Yang, Philippe Corboz

item.title: Entanglement and information dynamics in charged dual-unitary circuits with impurities
item.description: arXiv:2611.18435v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Local parts of a closed, non-equilibrium quantum many-body system can reach stationarity through the buildup of entanglement between different regions. In this paper we investigate how this process is affected by the presence of a quantum impurity that breaks a global symmetry of the bulk. In particular, we study a charged dual-unitary quantum circuit perturbed by a symmetry-breaking, non-dual-unitary gate acting on a spatially fixed pair of sites. In this setup we calculate the entanglement entropy for a subsystem that does not contain the impurity, as well as the mutual information and logarithmic negativity for a bipartite subsystem that straddles the impurity. We obtain exact results in the early time regime for these quantities from the dual unitarity of the bulk system. Beyond this regime, we compute the predictions of the quasiparticle and entanglement membrane pictures, supporting them with exact calculations obtained by taking the corresponding limits of the bulk entangling power. We find that the presence of a symmetry-breaking impurity can lead to a richer behaviour of quantum relaxation, including non-monotonic evolution of the entanglement entropy, a modification of the long-time steady state, and persistent subsystem mutual information and entanglement negativity. This behaviour is understood in terms of long-range correlations generated by scattering from the impurity, and facilitated by the ballistic propagation of the conserved charges.
item.dc:creator: Shachar Fraenkel, Colin Rylands

item.title: Beyond Blossom: Accelerating MWPM Decoding for Surface Codes With Local Predecoding and Architecture-Aware Optimizations
item.description: arXiv:2611.18476v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) is widely used to decode surface codes, but its computational cost increases with code distance. We present Beyond Blossom, a state-of-the-art CPU-based MWPM decoder for surface codes. It combines algorithmic optimization through local predecoding, architecture-aware optimization, and pipeline-wide parallelism to reduce matching workload and execution overhead while preserving MWPM optimality. Across rotated surface codes with distances 9-33 and circuit-level physical error rates of 0.05%-0.3%, on a single CPU core, Beyond Blossom achieves a 4.23$\times$ geometric-mean speedup and up to 5.58$\times$ speedup over Sparse Blossom in PyMatching. At distance 33 and a physical error rate of 0.1%, with 8 CPU cores, decoding a block of 33 measurement rounds takes 21.40 $\mu$s on average, equivalent to 0.65 $\mu$s per round.
item.dc:creator: Jiayu Fu, Zirong Shen, Lin Gan, Yiming Zhang, Wenjing Han, Xiaoming Sun, Riling Li, Guangwen Yang

item.title: Unitary realization of wavefunction collapse
item.description: arXiv:1305.3594v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent quantum reconstruction projects demand pure unitary time evolution which seems to contradict the collapse postulate. Inspired by Zurek's environment assisted invariance idea, a natural unitary realization of wavefunction collapse is proposed using Grothendieck group construction for the tensor product commutative monoid.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: International Journal of Quantum Information vol 14, No. 4 (2016) 1640015
item.dc:creator: Florin Moldoveanu

item.title: Quantum Channel Testing in Average-Case Distance
item.description: arXiv:2409.12566v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the complexity of testing properties of quantum channels. First, we show that testing identity to any channel $\mathcal N: \mathbb C^{d_{\mathrm{in}} \times d_{\mathrm{in}}} \to \mathbb C^{d_{\mathrm{out}} \times d_{\mathrm{out}}}$ in diamond norm distance requires $\Omega(\sqrt{d_{\mathrm{in}}} / \varepsilon)$ queries, even in the strongest algorithmic model that admits ancillae, coherence, and adaptivity. This is due to the worst-case nature of the distance induced by the diamond norm. Motivated by this limitation and other theoretical and practical applications, we introduce an average-case analogue of the diamond norm, which we call the average-case imitation diamond (ACID) norm. In the weakest algorithmic model without ancillae, coherence, or adaptivity, we prove that testing identity to certain types of channels in ACID distance can be done with complexity independent of the dimensions of the channel, while for other types of channels the complexity depends on both the input and output dimensions. Building on previous work, we also show that identity to any fixed channel can be tested with $\tilde O(d_{\mathrm{in}} d_{\mathrm{out}}^{3/2} / \varepsilon^2)$ queries in ACID distance and $\tilde O(d_{\mathrm{in}}^2 d_{\mathrm{out}}^{3/2} / \varepsilon^2)$ queries in diamond distance in this model. Finally, we prove tight bounds on the complexity of channel tomography in ACID distance.
item.dc:creator: Gregory Rosenthal, Hugo Aaronson, Sathyawageeswar Subramanian, Animesh Datta, Tom Gur

item.title: Genuine multipartite entanglement as a probe of many-body localization in disordered spin chains with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions
item.description: arXiv:2507.22795v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) in a disordered system and its potential for detecting the transition from the thermalized to the localized phase. We demonstrate that the quenched average GME can approach its near-maximum value in the ergodic phase of a disordered quantum spin model. In contrast, GME vanishes in the many-body localized (MBL) phase, both in equilibrium and in the long-time dynamical regime, indicating lack of multipartite entanglement in the localized regime. To establish this, we analyze the disordered Heisenberg spin chain subjected to a random magnetic field along with the two- and three-body Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interactions. We exhibit that the behavior of GME, in both the mid-spectrum of the Hamiltonian and the dynamically evolved states from an initial Neel configuration, serves as a reliable indicator of the critical disorder strength required for the ergodic to MBL transition. The identified transition point aligns well with standard indicators such as the gap ratio and the correlation length. Moreover, we find that the presence of DM interactions, particularly the three-body interaction, significantly enlarges the thermal phase and delays the onset of localization with an extended correlation length. This shift in the transition point is consistently reflected in both static and dynamical analyses, reinforcing GME as a robust probe for MBL transitions.
item.dc:creator: Triyas Sapui, Keshav Das Agarwal, Tanoy Kanti Konar, Leela Ganesh Chandra Lakkaraju, Aditi Sen De

item.title: No-go theorem for maximally $\psi-$epistemic models using two pure states of a qubit
item.description: arXiv:2509.10437v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work addresses the fundamental question concerning the nature of quantum states, specifically to what extent they represent an agent's knowledge about the system, that is, is \textit{epistemic} in nature. We show that, despite the existence of the Kochen-Specker model, which is a maximally $\psi-$epistemic model for single-qubit systems when projective measurements are employed, \textit{no} maximally $\psi-$epistemic model can reproduce statistics arising out of non-projective measurements on a pair of single-qubit states. This has been done in an experimentally robust way using only two pure single-qubit states and their equal mixture, by constructing a two-input, three-output game called \textit{Risk Aware Distinguishability} (RAD) and generalizing the notion of epistemic and quantum overlaps using RAD. Furthermore, we maximize the difference of generalized overlaps instead of minimizing their ratio, and in the process point out why that is a stricter criterion for refuting $\psi-$epistemic models.
item.dc:creator: Sagnik Ray, Anubhav Chaturvedi, Debashis Saha

item.title: Dynamical error reshaping for dual-rail erasure qubits
item.description: arXiv:2510.08416v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Erasure qubits -- qubits designed to have an error profile that is dominated by detectable leakage errors -- are a promising way to cut down the resources needed for quantum error correction. There have been several recent experiments demonstrating erasure qubits in superconducting quantum processors, most notably the dual-rail qubit defined by the one-photon subspace of two coupled cavities. An outstanding challenge is that the ancillary transmons needed to facilitate erasure checks and two-qubit gates introduce a substantial amount of noise, limiting the benefits of working with erasure-biased qubits. Here, we show how to suppress the adverse effects of transmon-induced noise while performing erasure checks or two-qubit gates. We present control schemes for these operations that suppress erasure check errors by three orders of magnitude and reduce the logical two-qubit gate infidelities by up to three orders of magnitude.
item.dc:creator: Filippos Dakis, Shruti Puri, Sophia E. Economou, Edwin Barnes

item.title: The Quantum Agreement Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2511.21258v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Intersubjective consistency asks when different observers of a physical system, reasoning from a shared theory, will agree on their probability assessments. Classical probability theory provides a benchmark in the form of the Agreement Theorem (Aumann, 1976). We study the quantum mechanics (QM) analog to the classical Agreement Theorem in a finite-dimensional tripartite setting in which two observers obtain information via local projective measurements. We represent their mutual awareness by common certainty, which is formally an infinite hierarchy of certainty operators concerning the probability of an event of interest. We first prove that if the observers' measurements commute with one another and with the property of interest, common certainty forces their probability assessments to coincide, thereby recovering a QM analog to the classical Agreement Theorem. We then construct a one-parameter family of qutrit-qubit-qubit models in which one observer's measurement does not commute with the property and common certainty of disagreement occurs -- a distinctively QM phenomenon. The mechanism is coherence between branches distinguished by one but not the other observer's measurement. When measurement outcomes are stored in a classical register, the resulting dephasing removes this coherence and restores agreement. Finally, we prove that QM does not permit the extreme 0-1 configuration in which Alice is certain of a property and is also certain that Bob is certain of its negation. These results aim to turn debate in QM about observer-dependent facts into precise mathematical conditions for when intersubjective agreement or disagreement in QM can be sustained.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2026
item.dc:creator: Mar\'ia Garc\'ia D\'iaz, Adam Brandenburger, Giannicola Scarpa

item.title: On the Dynamics of Local Hidden-Variable Models
item.description: arXiv:2512.16682v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bell nonlocality is an intriguing property of quantum mechanics with far-reaching consequences for information processing, philosophy, and our fundamental understanding of nature. However, standard Bell nonlocality is a statement about correlations at a fixed point in time only. It does not take into account dynamics, i.e., time evolution of those correlations. Consider a dynamic situation where the correlations remain local for all times. Then, at each moment in time, there exists a local hidden-variable (LHV) model reproducing the momentary correlations. Can the time evolution of the correlations then be captured by evolving the hidden variables? We make this question precise by defining dynamical LHV models and motivating additional physical attributes such as locality and continuity of the dynamics. We then establish a series of complementary go and no-go theorems that together map out which combinations of these properties LHV dynamics can and cannot have. In particular, noninteracting quantum dynamics can be represented on the hidden-variable level in a local way, but LHV dynamics can fail to exist for interacting systems: Even though the observed correlations are local at all times, their time evolution may nevertheless be incompatible with local hidden-variable dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Nick von Selzam, Florian Marquardt

item.title: Synthesis of Fault-tolerant State Preparation Circuits using Steane-type Error Detection
item.description: arXiv:2601.13313v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fault-tolerant state preparation is essential for reliable quantum error correction, particularly in Steane-type error correction, which relies on robust ancilla states for syndrome readout. One method of fault-tolerant state preparation is to initialize multiple ancilla states and check them against each other to detect problematic errors. In the worst case, the number of states required for successful initialization grows polynomially with the code distance, but it has been shown that this can be reduced to constant ancilla overhead-in the best case, only four states are required. However, existing techniques for finding low-overhead initialization schemes are limited to codes with large symmetry groups, such as the Golay code. In this work, we propose a general, automated synthesis methodology for Steane-type fault-tolerant state preparation circuits that applies to arbitrary Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes and does not rely on code symmetries. We apply the proposed methods to various CSS codes up to a distance of seven and simulate the successful fault-tolerant initialization of logical basis states under circuit-level depolarizing noise. The circuits synthesized using the proposed methodology provide an important step towards experimental realizations of high-fidelity ancilla states for near-term demonstration of fault-tolerant quantum computation.
item.dc:creator: Erik Weilandt, Tom Peham, Robert Wille

item.title: Prodiabatic Elimination: Higher Order Elimination of Fast Variables with Quantum Noise
item.description: arXiv:2602.21896v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Adiabatic elimination plays a central role in cavity quantum electrodynamics by removing fast cavity degrees of freedom, but at the cost of losing their finite-time response in multi-time correlations. We introduce prodiabatic elimination, a systematic expansion of the quantum Langevin equations that retains vacuum-noise contributions alongside higher-order corrections to the eliminated cavity field. This provides controlled access to arbitrary time- and normally ordered multi-time correlation functions, including photodetection observables, beyond what can be recovered from effective atomic dynamics alone. In the driven-dissipative Jaynes-Cummings model, we identify a vacuum-mediated effective repulsion between detected photons that suppresses short-delay bunching. For a single-photon switch, we analytically resolve a finite heralded response time arising from the cavity field's delayed adjustment to the atomic transfer.
item.dc:creator: Jan Neuser, Marcelo Janovitch, Matteo Brunelli, Patrick P. Potts

item.title: Digital dissipative state preparation for frustration-free gapless quantum systems
item.description: arXiv:2603.10119v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Preparing algebraically correlated ground states of quantum many-body systems is an important, yet challenging task for quantum simulation. We introduce a protocol that employs local projective measurements and unitary feedback for frustration-free gapless systems. Our approach prepares a priori unknown ground states in time that scales polynomially with system size. We analytically show the performance of our protocol for the dynamics of a single particle; we argue the same mechanism generalizes to many-body systems based on the physics of quasiparticles. Our theory predicts that the transient cooling dynamics directly reveals the system's universal critical properties. In particular, the state preparation time is linear in the inverse of the finite-size gap (up to log correction) when the system's dynamical critical exponent is larger than or equal to the effective spatial dimension explored by the quasiparticles. We verify these predictions in numerical simulations of ferromagnetic Heisenberg models in one- and two dimensions, a Fredkin spin chain, and a two-dimensional model of resonating valence bond states. Our protocol stabilizes gapless many-body ground states fully digitally without requiring analog rotations, enabling access to high-fidelity states beyond conventional adiabatic approaches in near-term experiments.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Feldmeier, Yu-Jie Liu, Mikhail D. Lukin, Soonwon Choi

item.title: Thermalization Across Scales on a Digital Quantum Processor
item.description: arXiv:2603.12236v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Thermalization of isolated quantum many-body systems normally unfolds via dynamical spreading of entanglement across progressively increasing spatial scales. The speed of this dynamical process, however, can be affected by the presence of local disorder. Here we study the crossover between slow and fast thermalization in a disordered two-dimensional Heisenberg Floquet model using digital quantum simulations with up to 100 superconducting qubits. Our experiment measures subsystem purities and $Z$-basis marginal collision entropies for patches of up to $3\times 3$ qubits. We resolve the onset of thermalization across scales by tracking each quantity's approach to its asymptotic value. In regimes where the system is moderately entangled, we validate our calibrated quantum simulations against state-of-the-art classical simulations. Near the crossover to fast thermalization, the classical methods no longer reliably converge due to volume-law growth of entanglement. By exploring this computationally hard regime, our work establishes a frontier of applications for digital quantum computers in probing complex many-body thermalization.
item.dc:creator: Faisal Alam, Marcos Crichigno, Elizabeth Crosson, Steven T. Flammia, Filippo Maria Gambetta, Max Hunter Gordon, Michael Kreshchuk, Ashley Montanaro, Alberto Nocera, Raul A. Santos

item.title: Implementation of non-local arbitrary two-qubit controlled gates via geometric quantum computation with Rydberg anti-blockade
item.description: arXiv:2603.17656v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the context of Rydberg anti-blockade, this paper proposes a new scheme for a high-fidelity controlled-unitary gate based on non-adiabatic holonomic quantum computation. Under specific detuning and interaction conditions, the scheme achieves a suitable evolution path for non-adiabatic holonomic quantum computation through reverse engineering of pulse parameters. This scheme can implement arbitrary two-qubit controlled gates with favorable robustness. We also evaluate the effects of spontaneous emission and laser intensity errors on the fidelity; numerical simulations show that the geometric gate scheme still exhibits excellent performance under these errors. Furthermore, we extend the local gates to non-local operations by combining entanglement transfer with auxiliary-atom measurements and classical feedforward, and demonstrate their application to interconversion among four-qubit entangled states (GHZ, cluster, and W states). This finding indicates the potential applicability of our scheme to complex quantum information processing tasks.
item.dc:creator: Le-Jiang Yu, Jia Zheng, Kun Pu, Chao Gao

item.title: Boundary-sensitive non-Hermiticity of the Floquet Hamiltonian: Spectral transition and scale-free localization
item.description: arXiv:2603.22746v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report a novel mechanism of boundary-sensitive PT symmetry breaking in one-dimensional Floquet systems. By designing a time-periodic driving protocol, we realize a Floquet Hamiltonian that is Hermitian under periodic boundary conditions yet acquires non-Hermitian boundary terms under open boundary conditions due to the non-commutativity of driving Hamiltonians. We show that boundary-induced PT breaking can occur when the boundary term couples Bloch modes that become degenerate after their quasienergy bands cross the frequency Brillouin zone boundary. For a single band, this requires the quasienergy bandwidth to span the entire frequency Brillouin zone, whereas in multi-band systems the relevant threshold is determined by the bands that can be coupled by the boundary terms. In the PT-broken phase, the eigenstates exhibit scale-free localization arising from the system-size scaling of the induced non-Hermitian terms. The associated wave-packet accumulation near the boundaries provides a dynamical signature of the transition. Finally, we present a general framework for constructing single- and multiband models exhibiting this phenomenon.
item.dc:creator: Bo Li, He-Ran Wang, Fei Song

item.title: Efficient photon-pair emission from a nanostructured resonator and its theoretical description
item.description: arXiv:2603.24351v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) in subwavelength nanostructures is a promising source of quantum light, owing to its multifunctionality and ability to generate complex quantum states. Nevertheless, the mechanisms governing photon-pair generation in such systems remain only partially understood. In particular, experimental investigations of key emission properties in individual resonators, such as directionality and spectral distribution, are still lacking, and predictive theoretical frameworks have not yet been experimentally validated. Here, we report the first measurement of the directional and spectral distributions of photon pairs generated via SPDC in a nanostructured resonator. Both distributions exhibit resonant behaviour, which we describe using an extended quasi-normal-mode theory. This comparison is enabled by photon-pair count rates of up to 0.45 Hz/mW -- to our knowledge, the highest reported for a nanostructured resonator. Our results provide new physical insight into nanoscale SPDC and represent an important step toward designing of efficient miniaturized quantum light sources.
item.dc:creator: Michael Poloczek, Alberto Paniate, Attilio Zilli, Vitaliy Sultanov, Yigong Luan, Tom\`as Santiago-Cruz, Luca Carletti, Marco Finazzi, Marco Genovese, Ivano Ruo-Berchera, Marzia Ferrera, Andrea Toma, Francesco Monticone, Michele Celebrano, Maria Chekhova

item.title: Scalable topological quantum computing based on Sine-Cosine chain models
item.description: arXiv:2603.25952v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a scalable framework for quantum information processing based on Matryoshka-type sine-cosine chains, a hierarchy of one-dimensional chiral-symmetric lattices obtained by repeated ($P$ times) square-root construction starting from the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain. A chain of order $P$ can host $2^{P+2}-2$ protected edge states, so a single physical device can encode a qudit of equivalent dimension (or, equivalently, several independent qubits) instead of one qubit per device. We show that (i) the adiabatic defect-transfer step underlying SSH-based topological gates carries over unchanged to the Matryoshka chain, transferring the full set of defect states simultaneously; (ii) a Y-junction braiding protocol then composes single-qudit gate operations in all energy sectors at once, increasing the operation density per physical device; and (iii) the same edge states provide a quantum memory whose capacity scales exponentially with the chain order at fixed physical length. Numerical fidelity analysis under on-site, hopping, and correlated angle disorder shows partial, chiral-symmetry-protected robustness.
item.dc:creator: A. Lykholat, G. F. Moreira, I. R. Martins, D. Sousa, A. M. Marques, R. G. Dias

item.title: Quantum simulation of a nonuniform Dicke model in a two-dimensional trapped-ion crystal
item.description: arXiv:2603.27627v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existing experimental realizations of the Dicke model in atomic or ionic systems are based on global observables assuming uniform spin-boson coupling, while inevitable experimental nonuniformity on the one hand requires site-resolved measurement of spin states, and on the other hand provides potential quantum advantage in simulating multi-spin distributions. Here we report the quantum simulation of a nonuniform Dicke-like model, due to either the inevitable experimental imperfection or the engineered spin-phonon coupling pattern, in a two-dimensional (2D) crystal of up to 200 ions. We explicitly demonstrate the sensitivity of few-spin observables and multi-spin distributions to the spatial inhomogeneity of the model, and examine the relaxation dynamics of the nonuniform model by measuring the subsystem entropies of selected ion groups. Our work enables the study of Dicke-like models beyond the symmetric subspace, paving the way toward understanding the role of nonuniformity in its thermalization and quantum chaos behavior.
item.dc:creator: S. -A. Guo, J. Ye, J. -Y. Tan, Z. -W. Zhang, L. Zhang, Y. -Y. Chen, Y. -L. Xu, C. Zhang, Y. Jiang, B. -X. Qi, L. He, Z. -C. Zhou, Y. -K. Wu, L. -M. Duan

item.title: Minimizing classical resources in variational measurement-based quantum computation for generative modeling
item.description: arXiv:2604.11578v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) is a framework for quantum information processing in which a computational task is carried out through one-qubit measurements on a highly entangled resource state. Due to the indeterminacy of the outcomes of a quantum measurement, the random outcomes of these operations, if not corrected, yield a variational quantum channel family. Traditionally, this randomness is corrected through classical processing in order to ensure deterministic unitary computations. Recently, variational measurement-based quantum computation (VMBQC) has been introduced to exploit this measurement-induced randomness to gain an advantage in generative modeling. A limitation of this approach is that the corresponding channel model has twice as many parameters compared to the unitary model, scaling as $N \times D$, where $N$ is the number of logical qubits (width) and $D$ is the depth of the VMBQC model. This can often make optimization more difficult and may lead to poorly trainable models. In this paper, we present a restricted VMBQC model that extends the unitary setting to a channel-based one using only a single additional trainable parameter. We show, both numerically and algebraically, that this minimal extension is sufficient to generate probability distributions that cannot be learned by the corresponding unitary model.
item.dc:creator: Arunava Majumder, Hendrik Poulsen Nautrup, Hans J. Briegel

item.title: Distinguishability of locally diagonal orthogonally invariant quantum states
item.description: arXiv:2604.12808v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the distinguishability of quantum states under local operations with classical communication (LOCC), separable, and positive-partial-transpose (PPT) measurements, focusing on locally diagonal orthogonally invariant (LDOI) states -- those invariant under local diagonal orthogonal twirling. This class includes many important families such as Werner states, isotropic states, X-states, and Dicke states. We show that optimal PPT and separable measurements for distinguishing LDOI states can always be taken to be LDOI, and the LOCC supremum can be approached by LDOI LOCC POVMs, enabling a dimensional reduction from $n^4$ to $O(n^2)$ in the associated optimization problems. We establish efficiently computable bounds on the distinguishability of orthonormal LDOI bases and prove that for a broad class of such bases -- including all two-qubit cases -- the LOCC supremum equals the PPT and separable optima. More generally, we show the gap between PPT and LOCC distinguishability is at most $(n-2)/(2n^2)$ for local dimension $n$.
item.dc:creator: Nathaniel Johnston, Vincent Russo

item.title: Lagrange: Operating Italy's First Publicly-Accessible Quantum Computer for Research and Education
item.description: arXiv:2604.21695v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe the design, implementation, and nine-month operational experience of the software management stack for Lagrange, an IQM Spark five-qubit superconducting quantum computer jointly acquired by LINKS Foundation, Politecnico di Torino and the Italian National Institute of Metrological Research (INRiM), and managed by LINKS. Lagrange is, to our knowledge, the first quantum computer in Italy that is fully operational and accessible to students and researchers from multiple institutions under formal service agreements, and to the general public under commercial agreements. When installed in mid-2025, the IQM Spark hardware was delivered by the vendor with authentication only: no billing, project management or fair usage enforcement were provided. We developed a modular middleware layer that filled that gap without modifying any vendor client software, by intercepting API calls through a proxy that enforces project-based budgets, reservation-aware authorisation, and per-user fairness policies. The middleware adopts a plugin architecture that cleanly separates vendor-specific logic from site-specific policies, enabling reuse across different quantum hardware backends and deployment contexts. Since entering production in September 2025, the system has processed over 240,000 quantum jobs totalling more than 1 week of QPU execution time, with greater than 98% uptime. Notably, students at Politecnico di Torino regularly use the machine during both lectures and formal examinations -- a practice we believe to be unique in Europe. We report on the system architecture, the operational lessons learned, and the infrastructure choices that made this deployment possible.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Viviani, Fabrizio Bertone, Giacomo Vitali, Emanuele Dri, Federico Stirano, Giuseppe Caragnano, Francesco Lubrano, Marco Cipollini, Martina Giovalli, Chiara Vercellino, Alberto Scionti, Virginia Ajani, Antonino Nespola, Olivier Terzo, Matteo Cocuzza, Bartolomeo Montrucchio, Giovanna Turvani, Gianluca Bertaina, Marco Coisson, Davide Calonico, Fabrizio Pirri, Pietro Asinari

item.title: Quantum limits on squeezing
item.description: arXiv:2604.22500v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In our work, we show how, for a network of bosonic modes, canonical commutation relations constrain the coefficients relating input and internal modes. Based on these constraints, we derive a lower bound on the total steady-state squeezing achievable in reservoir-engineered (dissipative) squeezing schemes, quantified by the sum of mode-optimal quadrature variances each normalized to its corresponding input variance. The bound on this normalized sum follows solely from canonical commutation relations and stability, and is saturated in the strong-coupling limit at unity. Furthermore, we show that adding independent parametric driving terms for each mode changes the quantum noise--gain balance and yields, for the same normalized mode-optimal sum, a distinct optimum bound, approaching 1/2. In addition, we show how these constraints allow us to reformulate the Duan inseparability criterion for a three-mode bosonic system in terms of a single parameter-dependent figure of merit. Our results apply directly to current electromechanical and nanomechanical experiments and indicate that the two-mode bounds can be experimentally approached even at room temperature.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Massel

item.title: Efficient ensemble randomization by tuning chaos in a nonlinear spin-1 system
item.description: arXiv:2605.27448v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present an efficient scheme to randomize a spin-state ensemble in a nonlinear spin-1 system by tuning chaos with an external periodic drive. Without modulation, the system exhibits a mixed phase space featuring regular islands embedded in a chaotic sea, where global mixing is inhibited by energy conservation. Using numerical simulations, we demonstrate that modulation of a linear Zeeman field not only facilitates transport between different energy shells but also drives ensembles toward a Haar-random distribution over spin states. Under optimized conditions, complete randomization at the level of the second moment is achieved on a timescale set by the inverse nonlinear interaction energy. In the overdriven regime, randomization is unexpectedly suppressed at specific modulation amplitudes, accompanied by the formation of sticky regions in phase space. We attribute this behavior to the dynamical cancellation of the leading low-order harmonic component of the periodic drive. These results illustrate how time-periodic driving can be used to engineer chaotic systems and achieve controllable randomization in nonlinear spin systems.
item.dc:creator: Jongmin Kim, Minsung Jeong, Jongyoon Han, Y. Shin

item.title: Quantum optimal control of steady orbits
item.description: arXiv:2606.15383v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Periodically driven dissipative systems can settle into steady orbits - fixed infinite loops on their dynamical manifolds. In quantum mechanics, steady orbits occur in cooling engines, lasers and masers, precision metrology devices, and magnetic resonance. Steady orbits and stroboscopic steady states are a promising target for quantum optimal control, but the numerical complexity is prohibitive: infinite loops defeat state-of-the-art algorithms that use explicit numerical propagation in the time domain. We report a solution to this problem and introduce a numerically efficient quantum optimal control algorithm for steady orbits. We use this algorithm to design microwave pulse sequences that dynamically polarise nuclear spins and enhance their magnetic resonance signals, while taking into account instrumental distortions. Improved performance relative to leading current methods is demonstrated experimentally.
item.dc:creator: Shebha Anandhi Jegadeesan, Yujie Zhao, Robert Hunter, Hassane El Mkami, Maximilian Keitel, Callum Musselwhite, Graham Smith, Guinevere Mathies, Ilya Kuprov

item.title: Universal photon blockade via two-photon light-matter interaction at chiral exceptional points
item.description: arXiv:2606.18756v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The photon blockade (PB) effect is a hallmark non-classical phenomenon in quantum optics and finds important applications for building quantum sources, while the control of PB by the non-Hermitian exceptional points remains largely unexplored. In this work, we theoretically investigate universal photon blockade in a microcavity harboring chiral exceptional points (CEPs) for building multiplexing quantum sources with nonreciprocal photon statistics. The results reveal that the presence of the CEPs leads to a stark contrast in the photon statistics of two whispering-gallery modes with opposite propagating directions. That is, one mode exhibits a strong PB effect while the other displays either sub-Poissonian or super-Poissonian distribution. Our findings thus may pave the way for advanced applications of photon blockade, and provide a theoretical foundation for the selective generation of single-photon and two-photon emission
item.dc:creator: Hai-Tao Dong, Meng-Long Song, Si-Yu Zhang, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, Dong Wang

item.title: A Quantum-Classical Surrogate Model for the Collision Operator of the Lattice Boltzmann Method
item.description: arXiv:2606.31351v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a hybrid approach utilising a quantum machine learning surrogate model to approximate the non-linear collision dynamics of the LBM. It offloads the non-unitary operations that challenge pure quantum solvers. The surrogate's expressivity relies on variational quantum circuits that implement partial Fourier series, while data re-uploading extends the representable frequency spectrum. Unlike previous approaches that use a fixed relaxation parameter, the relaxation step is embedded analytically in the circuit, allowing the learned equilibrium to be used for any relaxation parameter without retraining. We reassess standard VQC metrics, including expressibility, entanglement, and effective dimension, by relating them directly to task-specific surrogate performance and identifying the architectural parameters that determine approximation accuracy. The proposed surrogate is validated against the classical BGK collision operator using benchmark problems, including the Taylor-Green vortex for energy dissipation and the double shear layer for shear-driven instabilities and nonlinear flow evolution. Our results show that the surrogate closely reproduces the BGK reference on both benchmarks, using a single set of trained circuits across all relaxation parameters. These findings suggest that hybrid quantum-classical strategies offer a practical path toward realising the potential of quantum computing in fluid engineering.
item.dc:creator: Lukas C. Birk, David M. Wawrzyniak, Josef M. Winter, Steffen J. Schmidt, Thomas Indinger, Christian F. Jan{\ss}en, Nikolaus A. Adams

item.title: Susceptibility-kinetic uncertainty relations for quantum systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.01035v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Kinetic uncertainty relations bound current precision of stochastic processes by dynamical activity. The extension of these bounds to quantum systems has been impeded by coherence, strong system-reservoir coupling, and the subtlety of defining dynamical activity in the quantum regime. Here, we introduce a partial dynamical activity through the quantum Fisher information associated with the rescaling of the system-reservoir coupling and show that it bounds current precision via a universal susceptibility-kinetic uncertainty relation. The general validity of this relation is guaranteed by the natural contribution of a susceptibility term, which is experimentally accessible by tuning the system-reservoir coupling strength. We show how the partial dynamical activity encompasses previous definitions of activity in the weak-coupling Markovian limit and that it provides an information-geometric interpretation of correlator-based activities. We illustrate the tight constraint on precision that our bound provides with the example of the dynamics of a strongly interacting finite-size system and of steady-state coherent transport through a double quantum dot, where quantum effects invalidate previously developed kinetic uncertainty relations. We expect our bound to provide a powerful tool for optimizing precision in arbitrary quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Didrik Palmqvist, Janine Splettstoesser, Ludovico Tesser

item.title: Revisiting the invariant ring of two-qubit mixed states
item.description: arXiv:2607.23039v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Local unitary (LU) equivalence classifies quantum states up to changes of local bases and preserves their entanglement properties. Polynomial LU invariants provide an algebraic approach to determining whether two quantum states are LU equivalent. We revisit the ring of complex polynomial LU invariants on the full two-qubit operator space, equivalently the invariant ring under the local conjugation action of $GL(2,\mathbb C)\times GL(2,\mathbb C)$. For the two-qubit system, King \emph{et al.} previously determined a generating set of 21 invariants and the Cohen--Macaulay structure of this ring. Using a unified notation, we provide a self-contained derivation of the known Molien series and a systematic graphical reconstruction of the known generators. The Molien series is derived by explicit contour integration over the maximal torus, supplying computational steps not given in the earlier treatment. We systematically reconstruct the known generators using the graphical tensor method and provide explicit algebraic reductions of the candidate invariants. This work clarifies the calculations and graphical construction underlying the established results.
item.dc:creator: Bing Xie, Lin Zhang

item.title: Dual-Pilot-Assisted Frequency and Phase Recovery in Experimental CV-QKD
item.description: arXiv:2608.07277v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) offers high secret-key rates and compatibility with optical communication infrastructure. Locally generated local oscillator (LLO) architectures reduce security vulnerabilities associated with transmitting a strong optical reference, but independent lasers introduce frequency offsets and phase fluctuations that require accurate compensation. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a Gaussian-modulated LLO CV-QKD system over 12 km of optical fiber using two frequency-multiplexed pilot tones and RF-heterodyne detection with independent lasers. The proposed digital signal processing (DSP) architecture integrates CAZAC-based frame synchronization, global and subframe-wise carrier-frequency-offset estimation, and coherent dual-pilot phase recovery. We analyze 120 experimental frames, each containing approximately $10^6$ coherent states, and directly compare single-pilot and dual-pilot processing using identical acquisitions. The dual-pilot DSP chain achieves an average input-referred excess noise of $15.56 \pm 7.61$ mSNU, representing reductions of 28.1% and 17.4% relative to pilots 1 and 2, respectively. Under a trusted-receiver security model, the system achieves average modeled secret-key rates of $14.98 \pm 4.18$ Mbit/s in the asymptotic regime and $8.17 \pm 2.53$ Mbit/s using conservative finite-size parameter-estimation bounds. These results demonstrate the experimental benefits of jointly exploiting two pilot references for frequency and phase recovery in LLO CV-QKD systems, supporting their development for metropolitan quantum communication networks.
item.dc:creator: Christiano M. S. Nascimento, Artur A. Matoso, Gustavo C. Amaral, Guilherme P. Tempor\~ao

item.title: Heuristic Lookahead Distillation Protocol Search
item.description: arXiv:2608.13644v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bipartite qubit entanglement distillation is the process of converting noisy ebits into pure ebits using only local operations and classical communication. This is a core operation for quantum repeaters, enabling such crucial tasks as long-distance quantum communication and distributed quantum computing. In this work, we introduce a method for searching for entanglement distillation protocols and, using this technique, distil qubit Werner states at a higher rate than could be achieved using previously discovered protocols. In particular, we demonstrate the advantage of our new distillation strategy by improving the best known lower bound for the two-way-assisted quantum capacity of the qubit depolarising channel across a wide range of channel parameters, making progress in one of the long-standing problems of quantum information theory.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Barber, Stefano Pirandola

item.title: Qudit-ADAPT-VQE: an adaptive variational algorithm with counterdiabatic-inspired improvements for qudits
item.description: arXiv:2608.14981v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Variational quantum algorithms based on qudits have attracted significant attention in recent years due to their potential for more efficient quantum information encoding and processing. However, as in their qubit-based counterparts, challenges such as barren plateaus and the design of efficient ansatzes remain major obstacles. In this work, we propose to address these issues through a qudit implementation of the ADAPT-VQE algorithm, which constructs the ansatz iteratively. Specifically, we introduce an operator pool inspired by adiabatic evolution enhanced with counterdiabatic driving for ansatz construction and employ it to solve the Max 3-Cut and Multiway Number Partitioning problems. We show that the warm-start strategy inherent to ADAPT-VQE, together with an ansatz construction based on counterdiabatic operators, achieves higher accuracy than fixed-ansatz approaches and, at equal number of variational parameters, requires fewer native gates. Furthermore, we show that, in qudit-based quantum computing, ADAPT-VQE with a counterdiabatic operator pool can navigate rough optimization landscapes with local traps through the burrowing mechanism, suggesting robustness against local minima and providing a flexible framework for variational quantum algorithms with qudits.
item.dc:creator: Joaqu\'in Molina, Herbert D\'iaz-Moraga, Dardo Goyeneche, Diego Tancara

item.title: Improved lower bound for the two-way-assisted quantum capacity of the bosonic thermal-loss channel
item.description: arXiv:2609.27792v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The bosonic thermal-loss channel is a fundamental model for quantum communication. This Gaussian channel models the transmission of bosonic systems subject to both loss and thermal noise. It describes many practical systems, including optical fibres, waveguides and free-space links, where background thermal noise is significant. Determining the channel's two-way-assisted quantum capacity, the maximum rate at which quantum information can be transmitted reliably through the channel with two-way classical assistance, remains an open problem. Here, we improve upon the best known lower bound for this capacity for a wide range of channel parameters. We achieve this by combining an improved qubit-bosonic distribution technique with a recently introduced technique for discovering entanglement distillation protocols.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Barber, Stefano Pirandola

item.title: Approximate majorization and high-order capacity of quantum depolarizing channels
item.description: arXiv:2609.37240v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A central challenge in quantum information theory is to determine whether entanglement provides an advantage for information processing when coherent operations across multiple channel uses are allowed. For depolarizing channels, King's proof of the additivity of the minimum output entropy rules out such an advantage for classical communication at leading asymptotic order, while leaving open the possibility of an advantage for higher orders. In this work, we conjecture a majorization relation for the outputs of depolarizing channels and prove an approximate version of this conjecture.
